thread:
maria: pushing this up — support is getting multiple customer escalations for hosted inference in us-west1. Lots of 5xx + client-side timeouts. SLO alert fired ~10m ago. Customers report sudden error spikes and some auth failures.

chen: seeing the alert too. p99 gateway latency jumped and 5xx fraction crossed SLO. any traces? :eyes:

olga: traces are weird — sampling dropped at the edge. probe->gateway spans missing after 18:03 UTC. looks like trace coverage gap, not full traces. dashboard: https://console.redwood/infer/dash/usw1/alerts/1789991111

sam: logged an initial customer report: "500s on generation endpoint, JSON parse errors in body?" but they also saw repeated 401s then 500, so might be auth billing handshake flapping. I've forwarded full customer logs.

maria: ok, timeline: 17:58 UTC small auth-svc deploy (canary), 18:02 gateway p99 spike, 18:05 SLO alert. correlate logs for x-request-id across auth, billing, gateway.

kevin: running a quick logs query:
```
resource.type="k8s_container"
logName="projects/redwood/logs/gateway"
jsonPayload.httpStatus>=500
jsonPayload.route="/v1/generate"
timestamp>="2026-03-17T17:50:00Z"
| sort timestamp desc
| limit 200
```
Initial look: high volume of 502/504s around 18:02-18:08, upstream auth returned 503/timeout in many cases.

olga: traces that exist show gateway timing out waiting on auth: span operation "auth:verify-token" had >2s tails and then upstream cancelled. But note: several gateway requests have no trace id logged. sampling config might have been changed during the deploy.

deploy-bot: Deployment canary to service/auth-service v2.12.0 started by @jess at 2026-03-17T17:58:12Z. Canary traffic weight 10%.

maria: if the canary reduced trace headers or the connector lost header propagation we'll get trace gaps. but why 5xx at gateway? if auth returned 5xx or timed out, gateway bubbles 502/504. Could be auth overload or a regression.

chen: action items: 1) run a cross-service log join on request_id to confirm auth error -> gateway 5xx path. 2) check auth-service error rates & CPU/memory around canary. 3) temporarily enable canary fallback (route to v2.11) or increase auth timeout at gateway.

kevin: query for auth errors:
```
logName="projects/redwood/logs/auth-service"
jsonPayload.level="ERROR"
jsonPayload.err.message: ("timeout" OR "panic" OR "503" OR "rate limit")
timestamp>="2026-03-17T17:50:00Z"
| stats count() by jsonPayload.err.code, jsonPayload.instance
| sort desc
```
Results: spike of 503s on auth instances auth-3 and auth-5 starting 17:59, correlated with increased GC pause logs on auth-5.

olga: GC pause + reduced threadpool could cause auth to fail under canary traffic. tracing middleware uses a buffered header write — if GC pauses while accepting headers we can drop trace id. that matches missing spans.

sam: customers need a mitigation plan now — they want ETA. Should we tell them we are routing away from canary while we investigate?

maria: yes. immediate mitigation: roll canary back (or increase fallback to old variant) and adjust gateway auth timeout + enable a short-term retry (idempotent-safe) for auth handshake. I'll request rollback. chen, can you coordinate rollback with jess? Kevin, open an infra ticket to pin auth instances and check GC config.

chen: on it. pinging @jess and starting rollback now.

kevin: opened infra ticket #INF-4589 and changing JVM flags on auth service staging to reduce GC stall (temporarily -XX:+UseZGC -> -XX:+UseG1GC with tuned pauses). will run on canary replicate before full rollback.

maria: support message draft to customers: "We're investigating an auth-related incident impacting hosted inference in us-west1. We're rolling back a recent canary and applying temporary timeout/retry mitigations. Will update in 15m." Approve? :+1: / :-1:

sam: +1, send it.

deploy-bot: Rollback requested by @chen for service/auth-service. Canary traffic scaled down to 0% at 2026-03-17T18:10:04Z.

olga: after rollback latency and 5xx fraction trending down. traces returning but still lower coverage — will monitor for 30m.

maria: follow-ups: 1) add trace header propagation unit test to CI, 2) increase sampling retention for gateway spans for 24h to catch ephemeral issues, 3) evaluate auth GC settings and memory headroom for canary workloads, 4) add an alert for sudden trace-coverage drop separate from SLOs.

chen: logging the runbook steps we executed into incident tracker: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4589 - will assign postmortem to eng-sre + auth team.

sam: customer notified. they acknowledged and appreciate quick action.

maria: closing loop — if 5xx fraction stays below SLO for next 45m we mark resolved. tagging @olga for dashboard updates and @kevin for infra follow-ups. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
